chapter_theme: The five letters, the three letters and the one letter: Sivavakkiyar says the mantra is known only by one who has slain the wish for birth, that it is drawn in the root centre and heard as nada when inside and outside match, and that once known the letters are not the thing and yet are. Around this run the familiar attacks (bathing morning and evening, offerings to ghosts and village goddesses, raising hands to the god in a seen temple), a run of number-cipher verses on the tattvas and the muktis, and verses of self-knowledge: the eye cannot see itself, the unceasing conch sounds within, truth cannot be spoken in this world.
structure_note: No commentary orders the chapter. The mantra verses (1214, 1217, 1219, 1222, 1223, 1236, 1237) frame it; 1229 to 1234 are a block of number riddles; 1225 to 1227 are first-person verses of interior knowledge; the refrain விளைந்ததே சிவாயமே closes 1217 and 1236 and continues into chapter 66.

1214.reading: You who cherish deceitful birth in your minds and do not know the truth of the five letters: if you can slay deceitful birth, then you can come to know the truth of the five letters.
1214.nuance: The order matters: killing the wish for birth comes first and knowledge of the mantra follows, not the reverse. The mantra is not a means to end birth but what one understands once birth is renounced.

1215.reading: Bees that love the fruit of a grove with no unripe fruit, you eat honey no bee made and sleep night and day; before you board the sailless ship and land on the far shore, can the knowledge of silence be spoken by the mouth?
1215.nuance: The images are paradoxes: a grove with no raw fruit (all ripe), honey without bees, a ship without a sail; tradition reads them as knowledge that comes without process and the body or practice that crosses without visible means. The question at the end is the firm part: மவுன ஞானம், silence-knowledge, cannot be said.

1216.reading: You babbling ghouls who cry 'ghosts, ghosts': do ghosts take worship, does Pidari take worship, does the primal take worship, does the beginningless take worship? It is the body that is the ghost, and it took it, knowing its account.
1216.nuance: Pidari is a village goddess who receives offerings. The question who actually consumes the offering is answered by the last line: the body, which eats, is the real ghost, and it keeps count. The last line's syntax is loose.

1217.reading: In the root centre, with the three-cornered figure as its base, the mantra that rose in the middle of our Lord's four doors, drawn with eight petals, a cool blossomed figure: I see nothing else beyond it; Sivayam came forth.
1217.nuance: The verse maps the mantra onto a drawn figure in the body. மூலமண்டலம் is the root centre, முச்சதுரம் (three-square) the triangle tradition places there, நாலுவாசல் its four doors, the four petals of the root lotus in the yogic maps; the eight petals belong to another lotus (the heart) or the eight directions. தீட்டம் is unclear.

1218.reading: Seeking the first, running, running, morning and evening to the water; the channel that is the root of light, the pure space beyond speech, the Agama that begins with A, joined to the first ...: becoming difference upon difference, one is born and the body dies.
1218.nuance: Line 1 mocks the morning and evening bath; lines 2 and 3 name what should be sought instead: the central channel as the root of light, தூவெளி the speechless pure space, and the letters from A as the real Agama. நெற்பறித்தது in line 3 is unclear (paddy plucked, or perhaps நெற்றி, the brow); the fourth line gives the fate of those who stay in differences.

1219.reading: Sitting composed within the Supreme's five letters, rising and seeking, seated above, the mantra uttered: as one cuts bamboo, strips the fibre and works it into a tray, so it appears in the thread one has examined; cut through and realise it.
1219.nuance: The bamboo simile says the mantra's truth appears only after work, as fibre appears from the cane. நூல் is both thread and book, so 'the examined thread' is also the examined scripture; அரிந்து (cut) likely stands for அறிந்து (know) and keeps the cutting image.

1220.reading: If you can know, cutting through the cosmoses, the light that rose in the middle of the lotus, the wondrous Mayan who abides with the three circles, there is no raising of hands to the god in a temple you can see.
1220.nuance: The lotus is the heart lotus (the editors' gloss reads புண்டரீகம் as lotus), the three circles sun, moon and fire in the yogic body; மாயன், Vishnu's name, is used for the Lord. The claim is conditional: the knower has no need of the seen temple, not that no one has.

1221.reading: Rogue who dances in the halls at the crossroads; primal hero who stands as the lover within the lover; primal Lord who stands as the devotee within devotees; truth of truth who stands true to the celestials.
1221.nuance: வம்பன், rogue or troublemaker, is affectionate abuse. சந்தி is a crossroads or a junction; in yogic use, where the channels meet. The dancer of the hall is placed inside the one who loves him.

1222.reading: What is 'the Lord'? The mantra known and spoken. One who came in kindness, one who learned all the Puranas, one who came as Kannan, one praised for that cause: what is the One? The true mantra.
1222.nuance: ஏதடா, 'what is it, man', is a challenge in the familiar. The verse answers 'who is God' with 'the true mantra' and lists Purana-learning and Krishna's birth as either what the mantra is not or as its lesser causes; the syntax of lines 2 and 3 does not settle which.

1223.reading: Is it inside or outside, the place where life contracts and stands? You say you must come close and ask. When inside and outside match, it is nada; opening the hidden door, you must see the mantra.
1223.nuance: கள்ளவாசல், the thieving or hidden door, is taken by tradition as the gate of the central channel or the opening at the crown. The mantra is 'seen', not recited, and arises as sound when the inner and outer are equal; the question posed is refused in favour of experience.

1224.reading: The elements that whirled into being, the immeasurable wombs, the weighty gods, the flawless bond, the cosmos beyond ordering, world upon world: what is the body in which all these joined and burned and lay? Tell me.
1224.nuance: A riddle. The body that burned with all this inside it may be the universe dissolving at the aeon's end, or the yogi's body, which contains elements, gods and bonds and burns them in knowledge; the question form leaves it to the hearer.

1225.reading: Within myself, where did I run seeking myself? Because within myself I did not know myself; after knowing and discerning myself within myself, within myself there is nothing other than myself.
1225.nuance: என்னை, 'myself', carries both the self and the Lord within, so the last line says at once that only the self remains and that only he does.

1226.reading: As lightning rises from the sky and subsides into it, the Lord who is thought of stands within me, since he is in me; and as the eye appears from the eye yet the eye does not know itself, I have not known the me who stands within me.
1226.nuance: Two images: lightning that returns to the sky it came from, for the Lord who arises within and stays within; and the eye that cannot see itself, for the self that cannot be its own object. The verse ends in not knowing, not in knowledge.

1227.reading: Passing through the hall that cannot be contained though one contains it, love that cannot be contained though one contains it stays within me; lying or sitting, when affliction comes, or walking, the conch of nada sounds without pause.
1227.nuance: The hall is Chidambaram's, placed within; the sound heard in every posture and even in distress is the inner nada, the conch of 1211.

1228.reading: Garlanded with cool honey-wandering tulasi, anklets ... in sky, in earth and in the void, in the eight and the two, binding the mind with sweetness and holding it so that it does not leave: that is the joy of love.
1228.nuance: Line 2 is garbled. The tulasi garland names Vishnu. எட்டினோடு இரண்டு, 'eight and two', is Siddhar cipher: the Tamil numerals ௮ (8) and ௨ (2) resemble the letters அ and உ, so 'eight and two' is Om, and the mind is bound in it.

1229.reading: One release, three releases, four releases, joined with good; ripening in enjoyment, in merit, release other than release, as release; ripening as the serpent, as a bed, the fire that crossed the sea of good; ripened in sacrifice: what is it, primal God, that stood so?
1229.nuance: The numbered releases match the Saiva scheme of graded states short of union and the union beyond them. நாகம் ... சயனம், the serpent as bed, is Vishnu on Adisesha on a plain reading, or the coiled power at rest on a yogic one. The refrain என்கொலோ ஆதி தேவனே is wonder rather than a question.

1230.reading: Three and thirty-six, with three threes, as maya; becoming the threefold release, as three, three, three and three; the light that appears as three, a lamp that does not dim: how did it enter my soul, our Lord?
1230.nuance: Number cipher. மூன்றுமுப்பது ஆறு gives the thirty-six tattvas; the threes are read by tradition as gunas, malas, lights or states. ஆ (cow) in ஏன்று என் ஆவின் is the soul, as பசு is in Saiva usage, so the light enters 'my cow', the soul.

1231.reading: Five and five and five, and searching within what is not those; five and three and one: so the primal God stood. You who stand in all that was made of five and five and five, who can see you, who are five and five?
1231.nuance: The fives are the elements, senses and organs of the twenty-five; five and three and one may be the Vedas and the one, or eight. The firm claim is double: the Lord is these groups and is also sought within what is not them.

1232.reading: Six and six and six, five and five and five, the rising two and three, seven and six and eight: becoming knowledge of different kinds, truth together with falsehood, the sound that wells up: the Mayan who is maya.
1232.nuance: The number strings are unexplained; tradition reads them as counts of tattvas, letters or breaths. What is not coded is the conclusion: the Lord is the whole, including the false, and he is heard as sound.

1233.reading: Eight and eight and eight, seven and seven, eight and one and three: so the primal God stood. Those who bow at his feet with the eightfold prostration and recite the eight letters stand freed from sorrow.
1233.nuance: எட்டெழுத்து, the eight-letter mantra, is the Vaishnava Om namo Narayanaya on a plain reading, or the five letters with Om and bindu and nada on a Saiva one. எட்டுமாய பாதம் is probably the prostration with eight limbs touching the ground.

1234.reading: Ten and ten, seven and nine; by the good of gaining the land within the ten and four directions; with the ten ... that place, the primal Mal: release is release only for the devotees.
1234.nuance: The verse runs on the pun பத்து (ten) and பத்தர் (devotees). Lines 2 and 3 are obscure; பத்து நாற்திசை is the ten directions. The plain claim at the end is that release belongs to devotees alone.

1235.reading: Becoming the breath, joined in love, what came facing ...; living day by day in love, in the sins that good joins; casting them off and rising above, you made her of the shoulders nothing; loving your feet and never forgetting them, one may become immortal.
1235.nuance: The text is corrupt in every line. வாசி is read by tradition as the breath of வாசியோகம், the Siddhars' breath practice, though the word is also horse (1204); the one firm statement is the last line, that undying love of the feet makes one deathless.

1236.reading: Easily, in the body, is our Lord's dwelling; A and U stood there without perishing, and the kindling light rejoiced in that place; in the one that becomes space, Sivayam came forth.
1236.nuance: The two letters of Om and the light meet in the body and open into space, where the five-letter mantra 'comes forth'; the chapter's refrain. அளிவுறாது (without perishing) and கொளுகையான (kindling) are the uncertain words.

1237.reading: Devotees who speak of the five letters and the three letters: the five letters and the three letters are not that thing, see. After pressing the five letters into the heart and knowing that letter, the five letters and the three letters become that too: Sivayam.
1237.nuance: The three letters are அ உ ம, the five நமசிவாய or சிவாயநம. The verse first denies that either is the goal, then says that after knowing அவ்வெழுத்து, 'that letter' (the one beyond, or literally the letter அ), they are the thing after all. அவ்வுமாம் may also pun on the letter உ.

1238.reading: Because for the false, speaking lies is enjoyment, and because the truthful have no one true to hear them, there is no need to speak the truth; in this world I was afraid to open my mouth with the truth. Why have you made me waste away so, Lord Namasivaya?
1238.nuance: மெய்யர் மெய்க்கு இலாமையால் can be 'because the truthful lack truth' or 'because truth lacks truthful hearers'. The verse is a complaint, not a rule: the fear of speaking truth is confessed to the Lord as his doing.

links.note: Both put the cutting of birth before the mantra. Tirumular says the five letters show the way of grace to those who have cut the reckoning of the womb's way; Sivavakkiyar says the truth of the five letters can be known only by one who has slain deceitful birth.

Sivavakkiyar asks whether the knowledge of silence can be spoken by the mouth at all; Tirumular distinguishes true silence, in which speech and mind are both still, from mere muteness. Tirumular's distinction qualifies the claim: unsayability is not the point, the stilled mind is.

Both place a triangle at the root of the body: Tirumular's twisting in the triangle at the root with the two channels leads to the Lord's feet; Sivavakkiyar's mantra rises in the root centre whose base is the முச்சதுரம், the three-cornered figure.

Tirumular makes the heart the great temple, the body the shrine and the soul the linga; Sivavakkiyar says the one who knows the light in the heart lotus has no need to raise hands to the god in a seen temple. Both locate the temple in the body.

Tirumular lists lamps, flowers, sweeping and bathing the image as the servant's path to the Lord; Sivavakkiyar says the knower does not raise his hands to the god in a seen temple. The conflict holds if 1220 means that temple worship is useless; if it means only that the knower has passed beyond it, Tirumular's path remains for those who have not.

Both use the eye that sees everything but cannot see itself. Tirumular uses it for the Lord, who sees all and is not seen; Sivavakkiyar for the self, which cannot be its own object, so that he has not known the one who stands within him.

Both hear the unceasing sound within and see the hall there: Tirumular's ringing bell is the lamp of the inner breath, and he heard the sound and saw the hall; Sivavakkiyar's conch of nada sounds whether he lies, sits or walks, inside the hall that cannot be contained.

Both say the mantra's letters are not the end. Tirumular: when nama falls away there is no more seeking, and to join the great silence that is Siva is release; Sivavakkiyar: the five letters and the three are not that thing, until 'that letter' is known, when they become it.

1189 gives each letter of Om and of Sivayam a cosmic function, creation, form, delusion, clarity; 1237 says the three letters and the five are not the thing itself. The second verse keeps the letters from being taken as the goal that the first seems to make them.

Tirumular says to speak the truth as well as one can; Sivavakkiyar says there is no need to speak the truth, because the false enjoy lies and the truthful have no hearers, and confesses that he was afraid to open his mouth. The conflict holds if 1238 is a settled claim; if it is a complaint to the Lord about his own fear, the two need not clash.

new_concepts.gloss: the breath as the Siddhars' practice (வாசியோகம்): the controlled breath that is ridden like a horse, the word also meaning horse
new_concepts.label_source: the verses use the word (1235, as tradition reads it; in 1204 it means horse)

source_issues: 1235 is corrupt in every line (தென்னுக, ததோளி யில்லையாக்கி னாய்கழல்); only the last line reads cleanly.
1218 line 3 நெற்பறித்தது is unclear and may be corrupt.
1219 line 4 அரிந்துணர்ந்து is probably அறிந்துணர்ந்து, as in 1211, 1239 and 1242.
1230 line 4 ஏன்றெனாவின் is an unclear sandhi (perhaps ஏன்று என் ஆவின்).
1234 lines 2 and 3 (பத்துமாய கொத்தமோடும் அத்தலமிக் காதிமால்) do not parse.
